walkthroughs.body_html:
The lens changes shape to focus light.

Near object: ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments loosen, lens becomes fat and round.

Far object: ciliary muscles relax, ligaments pull tight, lens becomes thin and flat.

Myopia (short sight): image forms in front of the retina. Fixed with a concave (diverging) lens.

Hyperopia (long sight): image forms behind the retina. Fixed with a convex (converging) lens.

Other options: contact lenses, laser eye surgery, or replacement lenses.

The thermoregulatory centre in the brain monitors blood temperature.

Too hot: sweating (evaporation cools you), vasodilation, hairs lie flat.

Too cold: shivering (muscles release heat), vasoconstriction, hairs stand up to trap a warm air layer.

mcqs.q: How does sweating help cool you down?
options: Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Evaporation of sweat absorbs energy (latent heat) from the skin, lowering body temperature.
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Sweat is cold and directly cools the skin on contact.

mcqs.q: What does negative feedback do in homeostasis?
options: Negative feedback makes a process get worse or amplifies the change.
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
It reverses a change in a controlled variable, bringing it back towards the set point.

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.
